chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about a Muslim man who died, and for him was a Christian mother, and for him was a Muslim wife and Muslim children. So he said: 'If his mother becomes a Muslim before his inheritance is distributed, give her the one-sixth.'

I said: 'So if there did not happen to be a wife for him, nor children, nor any inheritor for him from the Muslims with a legislated share in the Book, and his mother is a Christian, and for him are Christian relatives, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book had they been Muslims. For whom would the inheritance be?'

He said: 'If the mother becomes a Muslim, then the entirety of the inheritance is for her, and if his mother does not become a Muslim, and some of his relatives become Muslim, from the ones who have a legislated share in the Book, so the inheritance would be for him.'
And if no one from his relatives becomes Muslim, so his inheritance is for the Imam.
ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for a Muslim man with a Christian mother?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the mother’s conversion to Islam before distribution grants her the full estate if no other Quranic heirs exist, highlighting the principle that a Muslim inherits from a non-Muslim only if the deceased is Muslim. This narration underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the Imam (or the state treasury) serves as the ultimate heir when no qualified Muslim relatives remain, ensuring the estate remains within the Islamic community.
